title: Larry starting the night shift in the radio van
description: Larry, pen in one hand and eraser in the other, looks up from his work inside the radio van at the start of a twelve-hour night shift he worked alone. Behind him a whiteboard lists Vietnamese place names with UTM grid coordinates; the quarter-hour scheduling racks stand at right. His name tape — HUNNEW… — shows over his pocket. The picture was probably taken at night, he says, by Weaver or Chapman; he had a bunk in the van, and when the radio keyed he was on it — "Automatic reaction to radio when you are on duty."
researchNotes: Larry's own confirmation (Memories comments, 2026-08-15; archived as data/recollections/giscus-vn-0015-c18032414.json and -c18032583.json) of what the survey read from the HUNNEW... name tape. Working detail established: twelve-hour night shifts, alone. The second comment ties the Rosethorn 007 call sign — his lifeline off remote sites — to Captain Guegler, here spelled 'Guetler' (a new phonetic variant for the person record). The place/grid board behind him still merits full magnified transcription; what it implies about the headquarters question is kept in research/units/callsigns-and-units.md. 2026-09-12 (giscus-vn-0015-c18415735.json), with 'Location: Ton Son Nhut': photographer 'probably' Sgt. Weaver or Sgt. Chapman, and a bunk in the van — the night man slept at the radio.
